source_text: De anima contra Arianos (fragmenta) ΠΕΡΙ ΨΥΧΗΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΕΙΑΝΩΝ 10 Τί δ' ἂν εἴποιεν εἰς τὰς τοῦ βρέφους ἀναβλέψαντες ἀνατροφὰς, ἢ τὴν τῆς ἡλικίας ἀνάδοσιν, ἢ τὴν ἐπίτασιν τῶν χρόνων, ἢ τὴν τοῦ σώματος αὔξην; Ἵνα δὲ παρῶ λέγειν τὰς ἐπὶ ἐδάφους ἐκπληρωθείσας θαυματουργίας, ὁράτωσαν τὰς τῶν νεκρῶν ἀναβιώσεις, τὰ τοῦ πάθους σύμβολα, τὰ τῶν μαστίγων ἴχνη, τοὺς τῶν πληγῶν μώλωπας, τὰς τετρωμένας πλευρὰς, τοὺς τῶν ἥλων τύπους, τὴν τοῦ αἵματος ἔγχυσιν, τὰ τοῦ θανάτου σημεῖα, καὶ τὸ σύμπαν εἰπεῖν, αὐτὴν τὴν τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος ἀνάστασιν. 11 Καὶ μὴν εἴ τις εἰς τὴν τοῦ σώματος γέννησιν ἀφορᾷ, προδήλως εὑρήσειεν ἂν ὡς ἐν τῇ Βηθλεὲμ τεχθεὶς ἐσπαργανώθη, κἀν τῇ Αἰγύπτῳ χρόνοις ἐτράφη τισὶν ἕνεκεν τῆς τοῦ ἀλάστορος ἐπιβουλῆς Ἡρώδου, κἂν τῇ Ναζαρὲτ ἀνδρωθεὶς ηὐξήθη.
thought_title: Christ's real body: infancy, growth, passion, resurrection
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise against the Arians by pointing to Christ's bodily life—birth, growth, suffering, and resurrection—as evidence that he possessed a real human body.
pass_a_gloss: But what would they say, looking up at the nourishings of the infant, or the increase of age, or the extension of times, or the growth of the body? But so that I may pass over saying the wonders fulfilled on the ground, let them see the revivals of the dead, the symbols of the passion, the traces of the scourges, the bruises of the blows, the pierced sides, the marks of the nails, the pouring out of the blood, the signs of death, and to say the whole, the very resurrection of his own body. And indeed if anyone looks to the birth of the body, he would clearly find that having been born in Bethlehem he was wrapped in swaddling clothes, and in Egypt he was nourished for certain times because of the plot of the accursed Herod, and in Nazareth having become a man he grew.

choices.why: Keeps the plural and the concrete sense of feeding/rearing, matching the literal lane's demand for exact force.
Renders the noun's sense of growth or development of age without importing a modern developmental term.
The glossary does not cover this term; 'symbols' preserves the concrete token-like sense of the passion's marks.
Captures the epithet's force as a title of Herod the plotter, without importing the mythological 'avenger' sense.
Renders the aorist passive participle's sense of reaching manhood, matching the growth theme.

pass_b_english: What could they say when they look at the nourishings of the infant, or the increase of his age, or the extension of his years, or the growth of his body? And to pass over the wonders performed on the ground, let them look at the revivals of the dead, the symbols of the passion, the marks of the whips, the bruises of the blows, the pierced side, the prints of the nails, the pouring out of the blood, the signs of death, and, to say it all at once, the very resurrection of his own body.

Indeed, if anyone looks at the birth of the body, he will clearly find that he was born in Bethlehem and wrapped in swaddling clothes, that he was nourished in Egypt for some time because of the plot of the accursed Herod, and that in Nazareth, having become a man, he grew.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'ψυχή' as 'soul', but 'ἀνατροφὰς' here means 'nurture/feeding up'; 'nourishings' is archaic and obscure.
last_rejected.fix: What could they say when they look at the infant's nurture
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνατροφὰς = nourishings/nurture; archaic but within normal range, meaning not changed or lost.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'ἀνάστασις' as 'resurrection'; 'ἀναβιώσεις' here means restorations to life, but 'revivals' is weak and clinical.
last_rejected.fix: the restorations of the dead to life
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναβιώσεις = revivals/restorations to life; 'revivals' within normal range, meaning preserved.

last_rejected.why: 'Symbols' suggests abstract signs; τὰ τοῦ πάθους σύμβολα are the tangible tokens/proofs of the passion.
last_rejected.ruling: σύμβολα = symbols/tokens/signs; 'symbols' within normal range, meaning not changed or lost.

problems.quote: the tabernacle of the Word and God
problems.why: Reader may not realize 'tabernacle,' 'body,' and 'holy body' all refer to Christ's physical body.

problems.quote: the wonders performed on the ground
problems.why: Unclear what 'on the ground' means—miracles performed on earth? On the ground surface? Idiomatic Greek expression poorly rendered.
problems.fix: Clarify as 'miracles performed during his earthly ministry' or similar.

problems.why: Both refer to signs of the cross/passion but use different terms a reader may not connect.
problems.fix: Use one consistent phrase for cross-related signs.
